metadata.title: Choose the Smallest Useful Rule
metadata.description: Combine divisibility, repeated digits, prime factors, digit counts, and number properties in exam-style mixed problems.

content.text: Mixed number-system questions reward diagnosis. Ask what the target depends on: last digits, digit sum, alternating sum, factorization, place value, or magnitude.

Do not automatically calculate the whole expression. A repeated-digit number may have a known factorization; a divisibility question may depend on only two or three digits; a digit-count question may be solved by size bounds.
Let's combine magnitude reasoning with a digit-count question.

inlineData.prompt: Let x be the product of two numbers 3,659,893,456,789,325,678 and 342,973,489,379,256. The number of digits in x is
hints: Use powers of 10 to bound each number, rather than multiplying them fully.
The numbers exceed 3.6 × 10^18 and 3.4 × 10^14, so their product exceeds 10^33.
inlineData.explanation: The first number lies between 3.6 × 10^18 and 3.7 × 10^18. The second lies between 3.4 × 10^14 and 3.5 × 10^14. Their product lies between 1.224 × 10^33 and 1.295 × 10^33. A positive integer from 10^33 up to, but not including, 10^34 has 34 digits.

content.text: When two methods are available, prefer the one that removes intermediate variables or discards irrelevant digits. That is both faster and safer under exam pressure.
Now use structure inside a repeated-1 number.

hints: Start with the divisibility rule for the divisor in the question.
Check the smallest relevant part of the number (digit sum or last few digits) before doing full arithmetic.
inlineData.explanation: Sum of all digits = 12, which is divisible by 3. So, the given number is divisible by 3. (Sum of digits at odd places) - (Sum of digits at even places) = 6 - 6 = 0. So, the given number is divisible by 11. The given number when divided by 37 gives 3003003003. So, the given number is divisible by 37. The given number when divided by 111 gives 1001001001. Clearly, it is divisible by 111 as well as by 1001. Hence, the given number is divisible by each one of 3, 11, 37, 111 and 1001.

inlineData.prompt: Which of the following numbers is a multiple of 8?
hints: Only the last three digits matter for divisibility by 8.
Compute the last-three-digit remainder before checking the rest of the number.
inlineData.explanation: We know that 872 is divisible by 8. Hence 923872 is divisible by 8.

content.text: You have the full Number System toolkit: classify, factor, test divisibility, exploit identities, and reduce large powers to small patterns.
